title: Tamsin and the Verdict
premise: Seven years ago, the drowning of heiress Marguerite Verlaine was ruled an accident, and the town of Hollowmere buried its questions along with her. When concierge Beatrix Ashgrove receives a letter confessing to the murder — followed by a second promising the truth is still unfolding — she realizes the confessor knows her own secret: she saw something that night and stayed silent. As Beatrix digs through seven years of filed secrets, she uncovers that Marguerite's inheritance was rerouted through forged papers, implicating the very family who employs half the town. The killer is Marguerite's brother Julian, who has spent years watching Beatrix, and the second letter was bait to draw out the last witness: her. In the climax at the drowned estate, Beatrix trades her silence for justice, choosing duty over the love she'd begun to feel for Julian's son, and the verdict finally lands where it always should have.
about_author: Ivo Delacroix is the pen name of a former night-desk clerk who claims hotels are the best observation decks in the world. He writes mysteries in the small hours, convinced every lobby keeps a ledger no one has read.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of Small Sins
chapters.summary: Beatrix Ashgrove, POV. Introduces the Grand Meridian hotel and Beatrix's habit of filing the town's secrets. Establishes her quiet loneliness and pride in noticing everything. Emotional beat: controlled contentment with an undertow of restlessness.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes, One Hand
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. Twin letters arrive at the desk — one confessing to Marguerite Verlaine's drowning, one promising 'more soon.' The handwriting unsettles her; it resembles notes she once filed away. Beat: dread cracking open routine.

chapters.title: What I Saw That Night
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV, flashback braided into present. Reveals she witnessed a figure by the Verlaine boathouse seven years ago and said nothing. She burns neither letter but locks them in her private drawer. Beat: guilt resurfacing like a body in water.

chapters.title: The Verdict Everyone Signed
chapters.summary: Beatrix interviews old constable Ewan Pike at the hotel bar. He defends the closed case too quickly, hands trembling. First hint the investigation was steered from above. Beat: unease dressed as nostalgia.

chapters.title: The Returned Guest
chapters.summary: Julian Verlaine's son, Theo, checks into the hotel after years abroad. Beatrix recognizes his name and feels an immediate, dangerous pull. He asks oddly specific questions about the letters. Beat: attraction shadowed by suspicion.

chapters.title: Room 312 Keeps Its Secrets
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. She searches the hotel's long-term guest records and finds someone has been renting Room 312 under false names for months — dates matching the letters' postmarks. Beat: the hunter realizing she is also hunted.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Marguerite via recovered diary pages. Her voice is sharp, funny, increasingly frightened as she discovers money moving out of her inheritance. Beat: sympathy for the victim made vivid and alive.

chapters.title: The Family That Owns Half the Town
chapters.summary: Beatrix attends the Verlaine memorial gala under pretext of work. Julian charms the room; his sister Camille watches Beatrix too closely. She overhears a fragment about 'the papers.' Beat: power wearing its best face.

chapters.title: A Third Letter
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. A third letter arrives, addressed not to her but to 'the one who watched.' It describes her exact position at the boathouse window. Terror becomes personal. Beat: the file cabinet of her life turned against her.

chapters.title: Theo's Alibi
chapters.summary: Theo and Beatrix grow closer over late-night conversations; he offers an alibi for the murder night that is almost too neat. She wants to believe him and hates herself for it. Beat: love against duty, first fracture.

chapters.title: Ewan Drowns
chapters.summary: Constable Pike is found dead in the reservoir, ruled accidental. Beatrix recognizes the staging — it mirrors Marguerite's death exactly. The confessor is cleaning house. Beat: grief curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: Camille's Confession of Sorts
chapters.summary: Camille Verlaine corners Beatrix, admits she helped forge the inheritance papers but swears she never touched Marguerite. She names Julian as the one who benefited. Beat: complicity without guilt, corruption as inheritance.

chapters.title: Room 312, Opened
chapters.summary: Beatrix finally enters Room 312: walls papered with seven years of surveillance photos — of the hotel, of her. Among them, a photo of Theo watching her window. Beat: betrayal, vertigo, the watcher watched.

chapters.title: The Son Who Stayed
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. His chapter reveals he returned to Hollowmere suspecting his father and fell for Beatrix despite himself. He confesses he photographed her to protect her. Beat: tenderness inside a trap.

chapters.title: The Inheritance Trail
chapters.summary: Beatrix and Theo ally, tracing the forged trust documents to a solicitor who died conveniently in between. The money flowed through shell accounts back to Julian. Beat: two wounded people building trust from evidence.

chapters.title: What Julian Knew About Me
chapters.summary: Beatrix confronts Julian at dinner. He is urbane, terrifyingly informed about her silence seven years ago, and offers her a job, a future, complicity. Beat: seduction of power, refusal hardening.

chapters.title: The Fire in the Archive
chapters.summary: The hotel's record room burns overnight; Beatrix's secret files survive only because she'd moved them. Someone wanted her blind. She realizes the final letter must be coming. Beat: escalation, the past burning forward.

chapters.title: The Last Letter
chapters.summary: The promised final letter arrives: an invitation to the Verlaine boathouse at midnight, alone, or Theo pays for her curiosity. It's signed with the handwriting from the first confession. Beat: cold clarity, duty chosen over fear.

chapters.title: Boathouse
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV, goes armed with a hidden recorder and Theo stowed nearby against her orders. Julian appears, confesses freely — he drowned Marguerite when she found the forgeries, then built seven quiet years on everyone's willingness not to know. Beat: confrontation as confession, evil made reasonable.

chapters.title: The Verdict
chapters.summary: Climax. Julian turns on Beatrix; Theo intervenes; struggle at the water's edge where it all began. Police, tipped by the recording Beatrix seeded earlier, arrive as Julian tries to stage another drowning — this time hers fails him. Arrest. Beat: the witness finally speaks, and the water gives nothing back.

chapters.title: After the Gavel
chapters.summary: Trial aftermath in brief strokes: Julian convicted, Camille sentenced for the forgeries, the estate frozen. Beatrix testifies about her own seven-year silence and accepts its cost — some towns forgive, none forget. Beat: accountability as inheritance, bitter and clean.

chapters.title: The Desk by the Window
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV, epilogue. Spring at the Grand Meridian; Theo returns as a guest, honestly this time, and she lets him stay. She retires her secret files, keeping only one folder: blank pages for whatever comes next. Beat: love chosen freely, vigilance transformed into hope.
